chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad and Aḥmad, the two sons of al-Ḥasan, from their father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, who said:

Regarding the young girl when she first menstruates, blood may continue to be discharged upon her so that she becomes a woman with istiḥāḍah. She waits regarding the salat (prayer) and does not pray until the maximum duration of menstruation has passed. When that has passed, and it is ten days, she does what the woman with istiḥāḍah does, then she prays, and she remains praying for the rest of her month.

Then, on the second occasion, she leaves the salat (prayer) for the minimum period in which a woman leaves the salat (prayer), and she sits out the minimum duration of menstruation, which is three days. If the menstruation continues upon her, she prays at the time of the salat (prayer) in which she had prayed, and she makes the time of her purity the maximum period of purity, while her leaving the salat (prayer) is the minimum period of menstruation.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer affected here by menstruation and istiḥāḍah rulings
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةِ: a young girl who has newly begun menstruation
key_terms.طُهْرِهَا: her state or period of ritual purity
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ: the maximum duration of menstruation mentioned in this ruling
key_terms.مُسْتَحَاضَةً: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding

ai.seo_question: How should a young girl who begins menstruating with prolonged bleeding determine her hayd and istiḥāḍah for salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a young girl at the beginning of menstruation when her bleeding is prolonged and resembles istiḥāḍah. It explains how she distinguishes between hayd and istiḥāḍah by using the maximum duration of menstruation and the minimum duration of menstrual bleeding in order to determine when to leave and resume salat (prayer).
